newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister urges protection for Zaire relief.
newsitem.headline: French minister urges protection for Zaire relief.

text.p: A French cabinet minister who visited eastern Zaire at the weekend said on Monday only a militarily-protected relief operation could save fleeing refugees from being killed by advancing rebels or starving.
Xavier Emmanuelli said in a statement issued by his ministry for emergency humanitarian action that refugees at Kisangani and Ubundu were ill, exhausted and had food for only two days.

"Unless relief is organised and its security ensured, all of those people, men, women and children, are doomed sooner or later to die of starvation, exhaustion, disease or be murdered by those who have been hunting them down for more than three months," he said.
The United Nations agreed last year to set up a multinational force to help get relief to refugees in eastern Zaire but dropped the idea after many of the refugees returned home to Rwanda.
Emmanuelli said up to 40,000 refugees from the Tingi Tingi camp had arrived in Ubundu, 100 km (60 miles) southeast of the northeastern regional capital of Kisangani.

The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said up to 100,000 refugees had flooded the town, overwhelming the four aid workers there. Some 170,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees abandoned Tingi Tingi 10 days ago, shortly before it fell to the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire.
Emmanuelli said a French plane landed 40 tonnes of food in Kisangani on Monday. He was due to meet Zairean authorities and relief organisations in Kinshasa later in the day,

The mostly Hutu refugees from Rwanda live in fear of reprisals for the genocide of up to 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda in 1994. They have been forced ever deeper into Zaire by a rebel offensive since October.

The French daily Liberation published on Monday a report made last month to the U.N. Security Council by a westerner resident in east Zaire which alleged the rebels had massacred tens of thousands of refugees.
The unnamed man said he had seen mass graves containing hundreds of bodies in the Goma area and was told by residents that thousands more were buried in forests.
The French foreign ministry welcomed sending a United Nations delegation to investigate.
